title: Income from Other Sources
outcomes: Identify income under the residuary head including deemed dividends.
Tax casual income and online game winnings.

meta.exam_tip: For gifts, test relative status first, then the threshold for the asset type.

concepts.title: Scope of the residuary head and dividends
body: Section 92 charges income not falling under any other head. Section 92(2) lists specific items: dividends; casual income such as lotteries and puzzles; employee PF recoveries; interest on securities; hiring of plant with buildings where inseparable; keyman insurance sums; interest on compensation; gifts; and others. Income is computed under the accounting method regularly employed, with ICDS under section 276.

Dividend includes deemed dividends under section 2(40): distributions releasing company assets, debentures or bonus preference shares to the extent of accumulated profits, distributions on liquidation or capital reduction, and loans by a closely held company to a shareholder holding at least 10% voting power, to a concern in which he has at least 20% interest, or for his benefit — each limited to accumulated profits.
Dividends are taxed in the shareholder's hands; no deduction is allowed for expenses (including interest) against dividends or mutual fund units.
concepts.analogy: The residuary head catches what the others miss.
concepts.work: A closely held company lending ₹5 lakh to a 15% shareholder with reserves of ₹6 lakh creates a deemed dividend of ₹5 lakh.

concepts.title: Gifts and inadequate consideration
body: Section 92(2)(m) taxes money or property received without or for inadequate consideration. Money: whole amount if aggregate exceeds ₹50,000 in the year. Immovable property: stamp duty value without consideration, or the shortfall where it exceeds the higher of ₹50,000 and 10% of consideration (stamp value on agreement date if part paid other than in cash earlier).
Specified movable property (shares, jewellery, art, bullion, etc.): FMV if received free and aggregate exceeds ₹50,000; for inadequate consideration, the shortfall if it exceeds ₹50,000.

Exclusions: receipts from relatives, on marriage, by will or inheritance, in contemplation of death, from local authorities, from registered non-profit organisations (subject to conditions), under specified non-transfer transactions, and by a trust solely for relatives. Cost of the asset for later capital gains is the value taxed.
concepts.analogy: Free money above ₹50,000 from non-relatives is income.
concepts.work: A plot worth ₹8 lakh bought for ₹7 lakh from a friend gives ₹1 lakh of income.

concepts.title: Casual income and online games
body: Winnings from lotteries, crossword puzzles, races, card games, gambling and betting are taxed at a flat 30% under section 194 (plus surcharge and cess), whatever head they fall under.
No expenses, Chapter VIII deductions or basic-exemption adjustment are allowed against such winnings; a lottery distributor's prize on unsold tickets is still taxed at the flat rate.
Net winnings from online games are separately taxed at 30% under section 194, with TDS on net winnings.
concepts.analogy: Winnings bear a flat 30% with no relief.
concepts.work: A ₹5 lakh lottery prize bears tax of ₹1.5 lakh before cess even with no other income.

concepts.title: Deductions allowed and disallowed
body: Section 93 allows: banker's commission for collecting interest on securities; employee contributions remitted by the return due date; repairs, taxes, insurance and depreciation for hired plant and buildings; family pension deduction of the lower of one-third and ₹25,000 (default regime) or ₹15,000 (optional regime); 50% of interest on compensation (nothing else); and other revenue expenditure wholly and exclusively for earning the income.

Section 94 disallows: personal expenses; interest or salary payable outside India without TDS; excessive payments to related persons; payments above ₹10,000 (₹35,000 for transporters) a day otherwise than through specified modes; 30% of sums payable to residents where TDS defaults; expenses against casual income (except owners of race horses).
Section 95 deems recoveries of earlier allowed expenses or liabilities as income in the year received.
concepts.analogy: Deduct only what is permitted, never against dividends or winnings.
concepts.work: Interest on enhanced compensation of ₹6 lakh is taxed at ₹3 lakh.

viva.q: What is the treatment of money received without consideration from a friend?
viva.model: The whole amount is income from other sources if the aggregate in the year exceeds ₹50,000.

viva.q: Can basic exemption limit be adjusted against lottery winnings?
viva.model: The adjustment is barred; winnings bear a flat 30% with no deductions.

viva.q: Which loans by a closely held company are deemed dividend?
viva.model: Loans to a shareholder with at least 10% voting power, to a concern in which he has substantial interest, or for his benefit, to the extent of accumulated profits.

viva.q: What deduction is allowed for interest on compensation?
viva.model: Fifty percent of the interest, with no other deduction.
Amounts later recovered for expenses or liabilities earlier allowed are deemed income in the year of receipt.
